corrections.correction_summary: CAPP continuation must use one dependency-ordered transition, structured completion evidence, targeted validation, and connector-safe state projection instead of duplicate completion PRs or prose-sensitive checks.
corrections.failure_summary: CAPP-01 and CAPP-02 incurred repeated full CI fanout, completion-recovery loops, safety-wrapper retries, and exact-wording validator failures that added large avoidable latency.

proposed_case.name: CAPP continuation uses structured single-transition fast path
proposed_case.setup: A completed CAPP item has exact-head CI and signed merge evidence, the next dependency-ordered CAPP item is planned, and repository access is connector-first with historical PPIA validators retained.
proposed_case.owner_input: Continue with the next CAPP item after approving execution hardening.
expected_actions: Bundle the prior CAPP completion projection with the next CAPP start instead of opening a standalone completion-only pull request.
Use structured receipt, checkpoint, backlog, commit, pull-request, and merge evidence rather than exact explanatory prose.
Keep closed PPIA feature workflows isolated from generic CAPP pointer and compact-status changes.
Use the connector-safe transition request path for coupled CAPP state projection when direct large-file replacement is fragile.
prohibited_actions: Run a second full completion-recovery pull-request cycle solely to copy already-verified merge evidence.
Require exact wording in selection reasons or merge messages to establish completion truth.
Trigger all closed PPIA feature workflows solely because generic CAPP runtime projection files changed.
Treat a safety-wrapper or GitHub Actions workflow-permission limitation as a content or validation failure.
proposed_case.pass_condition: The prior CAPP item remains completed_verified from structured evidence, the next item starts in dependency order through one coupled transition, only relevant validation is required, and explanatory prose can change without changing completion truth.
